statement: The 260-day calendar functioned not only as a count of time but as a divinatory and ritual system; Classic Maya calendrical cycles carried astronomical, ritual, directional, divine, and political associations.

sources.citation: “Ritualization, Ritual, and the Making of Meaning,” in Religion, Writing, and the Shaping of the Classic Maya World, Cambridge University Press.
sources.author: Cambridge University Press

sources.citation: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Living Maya Time, “Calendar.”
sources.author: Smithsonian NMAI
sources.venue: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian

notes: This records a documented ritual/divinatory explanatory framework alongside observational astronomy; the categories are not treated as mutually exclusive.
